fx_path.source: Egyptian pound per US dollar, FY2026E-FY2030E period averages. Built from the inflation differential rather than asserted: the pound averaged 47.74 in 2024 and 49.48 in 2025 (a 3.6% move) while consumer inflation ran far above the United States', so the real exchange rate appreciated. The path assumes that reverses only partially, at roughly 4% a year narrowing to 3% as domestic inflation converges on the central bank's stated 5% medium-term target

dom_pack_growth.source: Domestic packs sold, annual volume growth FY2026E-FY2030E. The company sold 244.3 million domestic packs of its own preparations in FY2024 and 291.8 million in FY2025 (+19.5%); disclosed capacity utilisation is 65% of 3,383 million units, so the volume is not capacity-constrained. The path steps down from a rate materially below the FY2025 outturn toward population-plus-penetration growth

exp_pack_growth.source: Export packs, annual volume growth. Export value grew 10% in US dollars in FY2025 (USD 54.7m to 60.0m) on a company that is already the largest Egyptian pharmaceutical exporter with 26% of national pharmaceutical export value across 67 countries; the biosimilars plant licensed in December 2025 adds a new export line rather than replacing one

dom_price_growth.source: Domestic realised price per pack, annual growth. Egyptian medicine prices are set administratively by the Egyptian Drug Authority and move in periodic approved adjustments rather than continuously; realised price per pack rose 12.6% in FY2025 after a much larger devaluation-driven step in FY2024. The path assumes price growth tracks domestic inflation as it converges on the central bank's target, with no real price gain

exp_price_usd_growth.source: Export realised price per pack in US dollars, annual growth. FY2025 realised USD 1.00 per pack. Generic export pricing is competitive and broadly flat in hard currency; 1% a year is a nominal-dollar drift, not a real gain

toll_growth.source: Contract-manufacturing revenue growth. A small line (0.5% of revenue) that grew 37.8% in FY2025 off a low base as the company let third parties use idle capacity

cost_shares.source: Audited consolidated financial statements for the year ended 31 December 2025, published in the company's 2025 Annual Report (eipico.com.eg -> Investor Relations -> Annual Reports), cost of sales note (26). Production cost of EGP 5,625.990 million splits as: raw materials 3,087.382 (54.88%); packaging materials 1,381.559 (24.56%); labour 447.415 wages + 55.497 benefits in kind + 46.342 social insurance = 549.254 (9.77%); fuel, oils, electricity, water and lighting 192.345 (3.42%); all other consumables and services 321.446 (5.71%); depreciation 93.498 (1.66%)

esc_materials_usd.source: Active pharmaceutical ingredient input prices in US dollars, annual escalation. The company's raw materials are predominantly imported active ingredients; they are escalated on a hard-currency price path passed through the model's own exchange-rate path, NOT on a domestic inflation index

esc_packaging_import_share.source: Share of the packaging cost line that is imported input (aluminium foil, film, closures) and therefore escalates on the hard-currency path; the balance is produced in-house by the group's own ampoule and plastics factories and escalates domestically

esc_labour.source: Egyptian wage escalation. Headcount grew 2% in FY2025 while the wage bill in cost of sales grew 27%, so unit labour cost is rising faster than consumer prices as the statutory minimum wage is reset; the path decays toward domestic inflation

esc_energy.source: Egyptian regulated energy and utility tariffs, escalated ABOVE consumer inflation for the near term because the subsidy-reform programme resets industrial electricity and gas tariffs on its own schedule; a domestic consumer-price proxy would understate it

esc_domestic_cpi.source: Egyptian consumer price inflation path, applied only to genuinely domestic service and consumable lines. Converges on the central bank's stated 5-7% medium-term target band

mkt_pct.source: Selling and marketing expense as a share of revenue. The disclosed ratio fell from 12.9% (FY2023) to 12.4% (FY2024) to 10.7% (FY2025) as the company got operating leverage on a larger sales base; the path assumes that gain is largely banked but not extended much further

rnd_pct.source: Research and development as a share of revenue, rising modestly from the FY2025 level of 0.75% as the biosimilars pipeline moves through registration

ga_pct.source: General and administrative expense as a share of revenue, held near the FY2025 level of 2.34%

prov_pct_permanent.source: Credit losses, inventory write-downs and other provisions as a permanent share of revenue — the FRAME A reading. Three-year average of the disclosed charge: 5.07% (FY2023), 9.24% (FY2024), 5.23% (FY2025); the average of the two years either side of the FY2024 spike is 5.15%, and 5.25% is struck marginally above it

prov_pct_normalising.source: The FRAME B reading of the same charge: a receivable and inventory book that is seasoning, with the charge decaying toward the 2.5% of revenue that a distributor-concentrated generic book carries in steady state. Both frames are carried through the whole model and published side by side; neither is averaged into the other

capex_pct.source: Capital expenditure as a share of revenue. FY2024 and FY2025 ran at 37.5% and 14.3% of revenue respectively as the EIPICO 3 plant was built; the plant was licensed in December 2025 and the residual construction spend completes in FY2026, after which the requirement falls to maintenance plus incremental line capacity on a plant running at 65% utilisation

cip_transfer.source: Transfers out of projects under construction into depreciable property, EGP million. beta.source: Own-stock first-tier regression: weekly logarithmic returns of the company's own shares against an equal-weighted composite of 36 Egyptian listed names built from the full covered price library, five-year window. A beta well below one is what a defensive, price-regulated, domestically-consumed staple should produce

kd_path.source: Forward blended cost of debt FY2026E-FY2030E in local-equivalent terms, continuing the central bank's easing cycle. The discount-rate glide takes its shape from this path by construction rather than being invented separately

rf_term.source: Terminal risk-free rate, built from norms rather than extrapolated: the central bank's stated medium-term inflation target of 5% plus the standard 5.5-point emerging-market real-rate convention

erp_term.source: Terminal equity risk premium, normalised below today's crisis-era level toward the rating-class norm; never held flat into perpetuity

kd_term_lc.source: Terminal local-currency corporate borrowing rate — the long-run Egyptian norm of roughly 10 points above the 5% inflation target

wd_term.source: Terminal debt weight on a net basis, NORMALISED but reconciled to the model's own forecast balance sheet rather than asserted. Today's net weight is 25.1%; at a 40% payout the forecast deleverages through the window, so a terminal weight at today's level would contradict the model's own trajectory. 20% acknowledges that an inventory-heavy manufacturer retains structural gross leverage

g_term.source: Terminal growth, 5% — an Egyptian-pound NOMINAL rate struck against a terminal risk-free rate that itself embeds 5% inflation, so the base case assumes approximately zero real terminal growth. Deliberately conservative for a company with a third of its revenue in hard currency and a biosimilars plant just entering service. Sensitised 3-7%

roic_term.source: Terminal return on invested capital, used to set terminal reinvestment as growth divided by return. The model's own FY2030E return on invested capital is computed below and this input is asserted against it

assoc_multiple.source: Earnings multiple applied to the equity-accounted associate stream in the enterprise-to-equity bridge. The larger holding is a 30% interest in a Saudi Arabian pharmaceutical manufacturer; 11 times is struck below the Gulf listed-pharmaceutical range to allow for the minority, unlisted and non-controlled nature of the stake

assoc_norm.source: Normalised annual associate contribution used with the multiple above, EGP million. The three-year average is 239.0; 320 sits between that average and the latest year, recognising a genuine step-up at the Saudi associate without capitalising one exceptional year

The median is struck at 19.5 and the lens is run across a 13-26 times band rather than on a point

peer_evebitda_regional.source: Median enterprise-value-to-EBITDA multiple for the same peer group. MARKET DATA, cross-check layer. Range run 8-16 times

narrative: [History] the audited consolidated income statement reconstructs line-by-line for all three years: revenue less cost of sales less operating expenses less the provision charge, plus associates, interest income, exchange differences and other income, less finance costs, equals disclosed pre-tax profit to within EGP 0.02 million in each year.
FY2023: revenue 5,232 · gross margin 44.6% · provision charge 5.07% of revenue · EBIT 1,225 (23.4%) · EBITDA 1,330 · net profit 823 · effective tax 24.0%
FY2024: revenue 7,591 · gross margin 44.9% · provision charge 9.25% of revenue · EBIT 1,529 (20.1%) · EBITDA 1,631 · net profit 1,097 · effective tax 28.3%
FY2025: revenue 9,441 · gross margin 44.0% · provision charge 5.23% of revenue · EBIT 2,366 (25.1%) · EBITDA 2,484 · net profit 1,458 · effective tax 18.8%

[Unit build] FY2025 sales of the company's own preparations were 351.8 million packs. Exports account for 60.0 million of them at EGP 49.46 a pack, which is USD 1.00 at the disclosed average rate of 49.48. The domestic book is therefore 291.8 million packs carrying EGP 6,286 million of revenue, EGP 21.54 a pack, against EGP 19.77 in FY2024 (+9.0%) on 244.3 million packs (+19.5% volume).
Production ran at 2,208 million units against 3,383 million of disclosed capacity — 65% utilisation, so the volume path below is not capacity-constrained.
Reconstructed channel revenue 9,302.469 against the disclosed separate-company revenue total of 9,302.469 — a difference of 0.000, which is rounding on the incentive lines.

[Consolidation] the reconstructed channel build is a separate-company total; the audited consolidated revenue is 1.0149 times it, the subsidiary's external sales. That measured factor, not an assumption, carries the build to a consolidated basis.

[Cost stack] every physically distinct cost line carries its OWN escalator: imported active ingredients (54.9% of production cost) and the imported share of packaging escalate on a hard-currency price path passed through the exchange-rate path; labour on Egyptian wage growth; energy on the regulated tariff schedule, which runs above consumer inflation; domestic services on consumer inflation. No single blended index is applied across them. Depreciation is excluded here and enters exactly once, from the property roll-forward.
Gross margin path (after the production share of depreciation): FY2025 actual 44.0% -> 43.0% -> 42.5% -> 42.7% -> 43.0% -> 43.0%

[Depreciation] the EGP 4,901 million construction balance stops being free. Transfers of 3,200 / 1,200 million in the first two years take the depreciation charge from an audited FY2025 118 million to 298 then 418 million. That step is the single largest mechanical change in the forecast income statement and it is a consequence of the company's own disclosed licensing timetable, not a view.
EBITDA (cash costs only) FY2026E 2,908 -> FY2030E 4,960 on Frame A; EBIT 2,610 -> 4,542 after the depreciation step.

[Asset-conversion cycle] the audited FY2025 balance sheet implies 268 inventory days, 129 receivable days and 54 payable days — a cash cycle of 343 days. The inventory position is policy: the company stated at its March-2026 general assembly that it holds a strategic raw-material stockpile sufficient for at least eight months. Working capital is PROJECTED from those three ratios, not plugged.

[Cost of equity] the quoted ten-year local-currency government yield is 22.31%. That yield is not riskless: it embeds the sovereign's own default risk. Subtracting the sovereign credit-default-swap spread of 3.41% leaves a normalised risk-free rate of 18.90%; adding beta 0.629 times the country equity risk premium of 9.41% gives a cost of equity of 24.82%. On the rating basis the same construction gives 24.71% — the two agree to 11 basis points, which is reassuring because they are built from different columns of the same source. Charging the raw 22.31% yield AND a country-loaded premium would give 28.23% and would count sovereign risk twice; that construction is not used.

[Cost of debt] the term-loan note splits the book 50% local currency / 50% hard currency. The local-currency leg is priced at 24.81% — the sovereign yield plus 250 basis points, and above the sovereign by construction. The hard-currency leg carries a 7.50% coupon but is charged at its LOCAL-EQUIVALENT cost of 12.34%, coupon compounded with expected currency depreciation of 4.50%. Blended marginal cost of debt 18.55%, 14.38% after tax.

[Cost-of-debt integrity] the company expensed 1,275 million of interest and capitalised a further 551 million into the construction balance in FY2025. On average gross debt of 8,999 million that is 14.2% expensed and 20.3% all-in. The 18.5% marginal rate sits inside that pair, which is the test: a marginal rate below the expensed rate or above the all-in rate would not be credible.

[Weighted average cost of capital] market capitalisation 21,947 against net debt 7,364 gives weights 74.9% equity / 25.1% debt and a starting discount rate of 22.19%. On GROSS debt the weights are 71.4%/28.6% and the rate 21.83%; both are published. Note the starting rate sits close to the quoted sovereign yield — that is arithmetic, not an error: the quoted yield contains default risk that the normalised build strips out and re-charges inside the equity premium.
[Terminal] cost of equity 14.90% (risk-free 10.50% plus beta times a normalised 7.00% premium); cost of debt 12.34%, 9.56% after tax; debt weight 20% -> terminal discount rate 13.83%.

[Discount-rate glide] the fractions are the cost-of-debt path normalised to its own endpoints — 1.000, 0.732, 0.439, 0.195, 0.000 — so the glide has the shape of the easing cycle rather than a shape invented for it. Discount rates 22.19%, 19.95%, 17.50%, 15.47%, 13.83%; the factors compound.

[Terminal consistency] terminal reinvestment is growth 5% divided by a terminal return on invested capital of 20%, i.e. 25% of terminal operating profit after tax reinvested. The model's own FY2030E return on invested capital is 18.7% on Frame A and 20.9% on Frame B, so the terminal assumption is not richer than the forecast that leads into it.

[Terminal weight] the terminal value is 74% of core enterprise value on Frame A and 74% on Frame B. That is high, as it is for any growing manufacturer discounted over five explicit years, and it is stated in the valuation summary and in the enterprise-to-equity bridge rather than buried.

[Book value and sustainable return] book value per share 37.00. Return on average equity was 24.6% in FY2024 and 26.5% in FY2025; the forecast settles at 24.6%. A sustainable-return multiple of (return 24.6% less growth 5%) over (perpetual cost of equity 14.90% less growth) is 1.98 times book, or 73.10 a share.

[Relative multiples] the company's OWN traded history is computable entirely from primary material — year-end closes against audited attributable profit: 4.7 times (2022), 6.6 times (2023), 6.2 times (2024), 9.1 times (2025), a four-year mean of 6.7. At 130.05 the shares trade on 15.2 times trailing attributable earnings and 11.9 times trailing EBITDA. The re-rating is the single most important fact about this share price: the earnings multiple has more than doubled against its own four-year history.

The lens triangulates three multiples rather than asserting one. (1) The multiple this model's own economics justify: retention must equal growth 5% over sustainable return 24.6%, so the payout the multiple can assume is 80%, and 80% over (perpetual cost of equity 14.90% less growth) is 8.0 times. (2) The company's own four-year mean, 6.7 times. (3) A regional peer median of 19.5 times — but those peers are Gulf-listed and face a cost of equity near 10%, not 14.9%; adjusted for that single difference the same median implies 9.8 times. Averaged on 6.79 of FY2026E attributable earnings a share: 55.58. Left unadjusted, the peer median alone would give 132.45 — the size of that gap IS the country-risk discount, and it is shown rather than hidden inside a chosen multiple.

[Normalised earnings power] the three-year average operating margin is 22.9%, against 25.1% in FY2025 — so this lens deliberately gives back part of the best year. Applied to FY2027E revenue of 12,942 million, financed at the FY2027E cost of debt and taxed at 23.5%, with the normalised associate contribution added, that is EGP 8.62 a share of sustainable earnings. Capitalised at the PERPETUAL cost of equity of 14.90% less 5% growth, on the 80% payout that growth rate permits: 69.33 a share. Using today's crisis-level cost of equity of 24.82% in a perpetuity would be a category error — a steady-state multiple takes a steady-state rate.

[Synthesis] four lenses, one field: Discounted cash flow — Frame A 86.06 · Discounted cash flow — Frame B 99.07 · Book value and sustainable return 73.10 · Relative multiples 55.58 · Normalised earnings power 69.33. Weighted centre 79.64; the field runs 55.58 to 99.07 against a 130.05 market price.

[The crux] the base build charges the new biologicals facility's depreciation and its interest — both mechanical consequences of the company's own disclosed December-2025 licensing — but carries NO revenue line for it, because the company has published no volume, price or utilisation guidance for the plant. So the crux is not what the plant is worth; it is how much it must sell. Solving the same model for the market price: an additional EGP 4,651 million of revenue by FY2030E at a 45% contribution margin closes the gap from 86.06 to 130.05. That is 20% of FY2030E revenue, or about USD 81 million a year — 0.81 times the USD 100 million the company says it invested in the plant. That number is observable: it is testable against the first year the company discloses biosimilar revenue.
